mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 5%, p > 0.05 (two-tailed t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) exceeding 2,000 since the previous month predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market expansion supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the labor expansion signal, with p-value > 0.05 in a regression controlling for FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (residential construction) of at least 10% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak housing demand reduces corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥10% in two consecutive months prior
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST declines by ≥10% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 triggers a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it signals supply-side softness and potential demand recovery.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return when INDPRO < 100 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) rises by more than 0.2 percentage points over the prior month, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to turn negative due to increased risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2pp in the prior month
regime_hint: Rising unemployment during a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite the unemployment increase (p < 0.05 for the opposite sign).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their prior month's levels predict a positive S&P 20-day forward return as dual demand signals boost earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month AND RSAFS > previous month
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not positive when both proxies rise (p > 0.05 in a two-proxy regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as labor market slack supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE remains below 4% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) below 203 for two consecutive months indicates disinflation, which is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as rate-cut expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥5 over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when CPIAUCSL declines as specified (p > 0.05).
